question: Does keeping the position's units and facilities in slot maps instead of std::maps keyed by name leave play unchanged, and what does it save?
machine: Apple M4 Max: 10 performance and 4 efficiency cores, 36 GB

searched_games.network: 64x2 networks with random-filled first-layer tables (tools/replay_coordinator_rounds.py --make-weights), evaluated one position at a time

notes: The bracketed searched games ran in the order: this change, the facility types build, this change, back to back on the same Mac, with nothing else of this study running.
Instruction counts of repeated searched-game runs of one build differ by about 1%; CPU seconds depend more on the Mac's other work.
A build with GWRL_CHECK_SLOT_MAPS (an iterator used after its map changed throws) played the same 300 random games identically, without one.

first_version.what: The first SlotMap found a thing by name with a binary search over its slots sorted by name, instead of the hash table of slots; same random games, compared with the facility types build
first_version.profile: /usr/bin/sample, 60 s of one searched game (seed 41) from 25 s after it started: the name search (SlotMap::position) took 9.38% of the engine's 21,641 samples for units and 2.07% for facilities
